clue.text: Log mania destroyed this tree

indicators.note: something destroyed is broken apart, so the preceding words are smashed and rebuilt in a new order

parts.note: the eight letters of the two words, taken together as fodder

explanation.surface: An obsessive craze for logging has wrecked a tree.
explanation.walkthrough: 'This tree' points back to the clue itself: the anagram is the tree being named.
explanation.definitionFit: The magnolia is a flowering shrub or tree with large showy blooms, a specific example of the general category.

clue.text: Partition seen to conceal a crown

indicators.note: to conceal something is to hide it inside, so one word wraps around the other

parts.note: taken as written
CR is a standard abbreviation for crown

explanation.surface: A dividing wall that has been spotted is hiding a royal crown.
explanation.definitionFit: A screen is a movable panel used to divide a room or shield an area from view.

clue.text: Dawn lies in bed, all shrivelled

indicators.note: something that lies in a place sits inside it, so one word goes within the other

parts.note: taken as written
dawn is first light, the coming of daylight

explanation.surface: A woman called Dawn is lying in bed, wizened and withered.
explanation.walkthrough: Dawn looks like a woman's name but is the daybreak, read as LIGHT.
explanation.definitionFit: Plants struck by blight wither and dry up, so blighted describes something withered and spoilt.

clue.text: Nearly kiss me to gain time: that's God's will

indicators.note: nearly means not quite all, so the last letter of the next word is dropped

parts.note: taken as written, before trimming
taken as written
T is the standard abbreviation for time

explanation.surface: A near-kiss buys time, and the speaker shrugs that it is all down to providence.
explanation.definitionFit: Kismet is fate or destiny, a Turkish loanword for what is ordained by divine decree.

clue.text: Gifted child shows stiffness of manner

parts.note: a gifted performer is a star
CH is a standard abbreviation for child

explanation.surface: A talented youngster comes across as stiff and formal.
explanation.walkthrough: Gifted reads as an adjective for the child, but it supplies its own noun, a star.
explanation.definitionFit: Starch figuratively means a rigid formality of behaviour, from the stiffening agent used on collars and shirts.

clue.text: Sarah, not tall, is a sickly brown colour

parts.note: Sal is a pet form of the name Sarah
something not tall is low

explanation.surface: A short woman named Sarah has an unhealthy yellowish complexion.
explanation.walkthrough: Sarah must be shortened to its familiar form; 'not tall' is not a deletion signal but a plain synonym.
explanation.definitionFit: Sallow describes skin with an unhealthy yellowish or brownish pallor, as from illness.

clue.text: Partners giving Capone false statements

parts.note: Al Capone was the Chicago gangster
false statements are lies

explanation.surface: Gangland associates are feeding Al Capone untruths.
explanation.definitionFit: Allies are those joined with others in a common cause or alliance, much like associates or confederates.

clue.text: Rhyming box for ice hockey players?

definitions.text: Rhyming box for ice hockey players?

parts.note: surface reading: a container with a sing-song name
setter's reading: the penalty area where offending players sit out, whose two halves rhyme with each other

explanation.walkthrough: The two three-letter words of the answer rhyme, and the second is a kind of box; the first names the offence that sends a player there.
explanation.definitionFit: In ice hockey and rugby the penalty box where a player serves time for a foul is called this informally.

clue.text: Craft to prepare mother and family in need of 1,000 pounds

parts.note: to dress food or a wound is to prepare it
an informal word for mother
one's family is one's kin
a grand is 1,000 pounds, abbreviated G

explanation.surface: A mother and her relatives are short of a thousand pounds to get a project going.
explanation.walkthrough: G stands for grand, slang for a thousand pounds or dollars.
explanation.definitionFit: Making clothes is a skilled handicraft, so the trade of tailoring garments counts as a craft.

clue.text: You can't say she's not fair!

definitions.text: You can't say she's not fair!

parts.words: You can't say she's not fair!
parts.note: surface reading: a protest that someone is being treated unjustly
setter's reading: fair means light-haired, so this woman's hair colour is being described

explanation.walkthrough: Fair here means pale-haired, not just; the exclamation is literally true of a woman with golden hair.
explanation.definitionFit: A woman with pale yellow hair is described as fair-haired, the feminine spelling of the hair-colour word.

clue.text: Army unit includes soldiers restrained by returning tiger

indicators.note: being restrained means being held in, so one piece sits inside the other
returning means going back the way it came, so the word is read from right to left

parts.note: taken as written, then turned round
soldiers are men in crossword shorthand

explanation.surface: A military unit contains troops kept in check by a tiger doubling back.
explanation.definitionFit: A regiment is a permanent military formation, usually commanded by a colonel and made up of battalions.

clue.text: Soft cry of dove by lake, lacking in warmth

parts.note: a dove's gentle call is a coo
L is a standard abbreviation for lake

explanation.surface: A dove murmurs softly beside a chilly lake.
explanation.definitionFit: Cool means somewhat cold, whether of temperature or of an unfriendly, distant manner.

clue.text: To sit alone perplexed, as in heavy traffic

indicators.note: perplexed means muddled and confused, so the preceding letters are jumbled

parts.note: the ten letters of the three words, taken together

explanation.surface: Someone sits alone, baffled, stuck in a traffic jam.
explanation.definitionFit: Cars queued bumper to bumper, each front close behind the vehicle ahead, describe a congested road in a jam.

clue.text: Dwarf means to achieve balance between extremes

parts.note: Happy is one of the Seven Dwarfs in Snow White
a medium is a means of doing or communicating something

explanation.surface: A short person seeks the resources to strike a moderate compromise.
explanation.walkthrough: Dwarf looks like a verb or a generic noun, but it is one particular named dwarf.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase names a satisfactory compromise or middle course that avoids going too far either way.

clue.text: Convict is entering face down to the right

indicators.note: entering means going inside, so this word is placed within the next piece

parts.note: lying prone is lying face downwards
taken as written
R is the standard abbreviation for right

explanation.surface: An inmate goes in lying face down, shuffling rightwards.
explanation.definitionFit: A convict is a person serving a sentence in jail, which is exactly what a jailed inmate is.

clue.text: Mysteries are still to be bought about Victory in Europe

definitions.note: the answer is an adjective completing the sentence, not a noun

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so the first word wraps around the abbreviation

parts.note: goods not yet bought are unsold
VE Day marked victory in Europe in 1945

explanation.surface: Puzzling goods are sitting on the shelf, linked somehow to VE Day.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition reads as a statement: mysteries are, by nature, not yet cleared up. 'Bought' may be a misprint for 'brought', but the wordplay works either way.
explanation.definitionFit: A mystery is a puzzle nobody has cracked yet, so mysteries are by nature without a solution.

clue.text: The bounty goes up as he signs a cheque

indicators.note: in a down clue going up means reading from bottom to top, so the word runs backwards

parts.note: a bounty is a reward offered

explanation.surface: The prize money rises each time a man writes a cheque.
explanation.definitionFit: In banking, the person who writes and signs a cheque, ordering payment from their account, is its drawer.

clue.text: A place for Rosie Lee?

parts.note: surface reading: somewhere for a woman named Rosie Lee, perhaps a seat or a room
setter's reading: in Cockney rhyming slang Rosie Lee means tea, so this is a vessel for the drink

explanation.walkthrough: Rosie Lee is Cockney rhyming slang for tea, the British national drink; the place is the small cup it is served in.
explanation.definitionFit: A small china cup with a handle is the vessel in which a cup of tea is drunk.

clue.text: Bargained with different tariff on mess deck

indicators.note: different means changed from the original, so the next word is rearranged

parts.note: six letters taken as fodder

indicators.note: to mess something is to throw it into disorder, so the following word is scrambled

parts.note: four letters taken as fodder

explanation.surface: Sailors haggled over a new price list in the ship's mess.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Mess deck' looks like a single naval term for where sailors eat, but 'mess' is the second anagram signal.
explanation.definitionFit: To traffic is to trade or deal, especially illicitly, so having trafficked means having bartered or traded.

clue.text: Finding no centre in clarifying agent

indicators.note: having no centre means the middle letter is removed from the word

parts.note: taken as written, before its middle letter goes

explanation.surface: A researcher discovers that a cleaning substance has lost its core.
explanation.definitionFit: Finings are substances such as isinglass added to beer or wine to settle out sediment and make it clear.

clue.text: Party chief reveals field of activity

parts.note: a do is an informal party
chief means main, principal

explanation.surface: A political party leader discloses their area of responsibility.
explanation.walkthrough: Party chief suggests a political leader, but the party is a social gathering.
explanation.definitionFit: A domain is a sphere of knowledge, influence or work, the area someone controls or specialises in.

clue.text: Moderate Tory politicians returning for a casserole

indicators.note: returning means coming back, so the word runs in the opposite direction

parts.note: Wets was Margaret Thatcher's name for the moderate members of her Conservative Party

explanation.surface: Centrist Conservative MPs come home to a hearty one-pot dinner.
explanation.walkthrough: In the 1980s Thatcher's critics within the Conservative (Tory) Party were dismissed as wets.
explanation.definitionFit: A stew is a dish of meat and vegetables cooked slowly in liquid, the same as a casserole.

clue.text: Paired community needs victory in race to enjoy

indicators.note: in means placed within, so the first piece goes inside the next

parts.note: the TT is the Tourist Trophy motorcycle race on the Isle of Man
a victory is a win
to enjoy a privilege is to have or own it

explanation.surface: A town linked with a foreign partner needs to win a race to have fun.
explanation.walkthrough: To enjoy here means to possess, as in enjoying good health.
explanation.definitionFit: A twin town is one formally linked with a town abroad for cultural exchange, so it is a paired community.

clue.text: Hatred shown by Wonderland Girl after getting married

parts.note: M is the standard abbreviation for married
Alice is the girl in Lewis Carroll's Alice in Wonderland

explanation.surface: The heroine of Wonderland turns spiteful once she has wed.
explanation.definitionFit: Malice is the desire to harm others, a deep ill will very close to hatred or spite.

clue.text: A climbing plant, long, narrow and in the hall?

definitions.meaning: first meaning: the ... bean, which climbs up poles

definitions.text: long, narrow and in the hall?
definitions.meaning: second meaning: a long thin rug laid along a hallway or corridor

explanation.walkthrough: The question mark admits that the second meaning is a playful description rather than a definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A runner bean climbs on canes, and a runner is also a long strip of carpet for a passage or hall.

clue.text: All the players dash out of bed

parts.note: a dash is a short line in writing
someone out of bed is up

explanation.surface: The whole team rushes to get out of bed.
explanation.walkthrough: Dash looks like a verb meaning hurry, but it is the punctuation mark.
explanation.definitionFit: A line-up is the list of team members selected for a match, or the cast of performers on a bill.
